A single trip's record cannot fairly resolve a repeat pairwise conflict in either direction, so the case must go to a human reviewer rather than be closed by the automated pipeline.

Escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal and, per POL-GEN-03, replaces any monetary ruling: the disputed amount is held rather than collected or refunded, and the rider's claim is not disposed of against the rider while review is pending. The fare breakdown shows the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee sitting at payment_status PENDING, charged_at null and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so an escalated file leaves the rider carrying no charge at all.

The in-app log shows the rider engaging on the pickup during the waiting window — 'Coming down now' sent at 06:51:40, answered by the driver's 'Okay, waiting' at 06:52:00 — and the driver cancelling three and a half minutes later at 06:55:30. That is a live coordination conflict between a repeat rider-driver pair, which is precisely the pattern POL-NS-09(c) reserves for human review instead of an automated single-case disposition.

EV-ADVIS-09110-01 is MISSING — issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, BLOCKING severity, weight_multiplier 0.0 — so no traffic advisory exists for this pickup road or waiting window. The driver therefore cannot credit any advisory-permitted accumulation under POL-NS-06(i): the in-geofence dwell stands on the trace alone, and no lawful-obstruction argument can be built on an artifact that carries no payload. I disclose the impairment and its issue code as POL-GEN-02 requires.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this dispute goes to a human reviewer and no money moves. The SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is placed on hold — it is not collected from the rider and not refunded to them while review is pending.

On the merits, the driver's account is well supported. The trip record carries an 'arrived' event at 06:50:20 and shows the driver terminating the trip at 06:55:30 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event, and the GPS trace places his vehicle about 24 m from the pickup pin — inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — stationary at 0 km/h for one continuous in-geofence hold running 06:50:00 to 06:55:30, i.e. 330 seconds against a 300-second minimum. POL-NS-01 limbs (a) to (d) are therefore all met. There is no false arrival marker (POL-NS-05: he was ~24 m out and stopped, far from the 300 m/15 km/h triggers), and no waiting-period shortfall (POL-NS-06), so nothing displaces the charge. The rider's device sat about 519 m from the pin, so POL-NS-04 does not assist them either. Left there, POL-NS-07 would pay the driver SGD 3.20 (80% of SGD 4.00), and the anti-farming guard is not tripped (1 no-show termination in 30 days, and 1/120 = 0.008 of completed trips, both below the thresholds).

That outcome cannot be issued, however. POL-NS-09(c) makes escalation mandatory where rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d together show 2 or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver in the trailing 90 days. Both records show 2, and the rider's own claim describes this as 'another dispute with the same driver'. Escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal and, per POL-GEN-03, replaces any monetary ruling — so the driver's compensation claim is accepted in substance but not paid out by the automated pipeline, and the rider's request is neither granted nor denied here.

The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09110-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) and carries no fact; it decides nothing, because the 330-second hold is a single unbroken interval and no accumulation under POL-NS-06(i) was needed.

Question for the reviewer: whether this pair's repeated no-show disputes reflect a recurring genuine pickup problem or possible abuse on either side — a question a single trip's record cannot fairly settle.

To both parties: this case goes to a human reviewer. No refund and no payment issues now, and the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is held rather than collected or refunded while the review is pending.

Why review is required. POL-NS-09(c) makes escalation mandatory where the rider and the driver have two or more no-show disputes between the same pair in the trailing 90 days. rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2 and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2 — the same rider and the same driver — and the rider's own filing says this is 'another dispute with the same driver'. A single trip record cannot fairly dispose of a repeat pairwise conflict in either direction, so the automated pipeline stops here.

On the merits, the driver's no-show case is otherwise sound. The trip record carries an 'arrived' event at 06:50:20 and terminates the trip driver-side at 06:55:30 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the required dwell and with no boarding event. The GPS trace places the driver about 24 m from the pin — inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — for one continuous 330-second in-geofence hold running from the first qualifying fix at 06:50:00 to the last at 06:55:30, which is 30 seconds over the 300-second minimum. POL-NS-01 limbs (a) to (d), POL-NS-02 and the limb (c) dwell are therefore met. POL-NS-05 is not engaged: at the arrival marker the driver was stationary at 0.0 km/h about 24 m from the pin, nowhere near the 300 m distance or 15 km/h speed trigger, and the in-geofence fix at 06:50:00 actually precedes the marker. POL-NS-06 finds no shortfall, so no refund arises on that route.

The rider cannot be exonerated under POL-NS-04. The rider's 06:51:40 message 'Coming down now.' was answered by the driver at 06:52:00, 20 seconds later and well inside the 120-second window, so limb (b) fails and the clause does not apply. The rider's device also sat about 519 m from the pin, over five times the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius. Whether limb (c) is affirmatively failed or undecidable on filtered fixes is moot, because limb (b) alone defeats the clause. POL-NS-03 is not in play: the driver was inside the arrival radius, not at a wrong face of the same venue.

But for the escalation, POL-NS-07 would pay the driver 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee — SGD 3.20 — and the anti-farming guard does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below 4, and 1/120 completed trips is 0.008, below 0.08. The escalation replaces that monetary outcome, and the reviewer will settle it.

The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09110-01 is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0) and carries no payload; neither side relies on it, and no accumulation of separate in-geofence intervals under POL-NS-06(i) is needed because the 330-second hold is unbroken. On the profiles, driver_profile.prior_no_show_flags (2) is a lifetime counter and context only; it took no part in this ruling, and the citable trailing-window figures were used instead.

For the reviewer: the open question is whether the repeated rider-driver conflict changes the disposition of the SGD 4.00 fee and the SGD 3.20 driver compensation that the single-trip evidence otherwise supports.

POL-NS-09(c) makes escalation mandatory where the rider's and the driver's records together show two or more no-show disputes between the same rider and the same driver in the trailing 90 days. The rider profile (EV-RPROF-09110) and the driver profile (EV-DPROF-09110) each report disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 2, and the rider's own filing says this is 'another dispute with the same driver'. That trigger has fired. Under POL-NS-09 the case is escalated and, under POL-GEN-03, an escalation is terminal and replaces any monetary outcome: the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is placed on hold - neither collected from the rider nor refunded to the rider - while the reviewer settles the repeat-pair conflict, which a single trip's record cannot fairly resolve in either direction. The rider's claim that POL-NS-09(c) applies is accepted and is the reason for this ruling; the rider's related point that the escalation holds the fee is also accepted, and I note the fee stands at payment_status PENDING with charged_at null and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so nothing has been taken from the rider in the meantime.

Because it matters to the reviewer, the trip itself otherwise reads strongly in the driver's favour, and I record that here rather than decide it. On POL-NS-01: the trip record carries the driver's 'arrived' event at 06:50:20 (limb (a)); the driver's GPS trace places all 34 fixes about 24 m from the pin, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and within the 25 m accuracy filter (limb (b), POL-NS-02); the in-geofence hold is one continuous 330 seconds against the 300-second minimum, a 30-second surplus (limb (c)); and the trip was terminated driver-side at 06:55:30 on RIDER_NO_SHOW after that dwell with no boarding event (limb (d)). On POL-NS-05, there is no false arrival marker: at the marker the driver was about 24 m away and stationary at 0.0 km/h, nowhere near the 300 m or 15 km/h triggers, and the first in-geofence fix actually precedes the marker. On POL-NS-04, the clause cannot run: the driver replied 'Okay, waiting.' at 06:52:00, 20 seconds after the rider's 06:51:40 'Coming down now.', well inside the 120-second window, so limb (b) fails and the rider's coordinate evidence never has to be reached. I do correct one point of the driver's case: the rider's device does read about 519 m from the pin, but no rider fix passes the 25 m accuracy filter (rider_qualifying_fix_count is 0), so limb (c) of POL-NS-04 is undecidable and neutral, not affirmatively failed - this does not matter, because limb (b) independently defeats the clause. POL-NS-09(c) displaces all of that.

Nothing in this ruling rests on it - the driver's 330-second hold was a single in-geofence run, so no advisory-permitted accumulation under POL-NS-06(i) was needed - and its absence neither helps nor hurts either party here. All four POL-NS-01 limbs are therefore made out, and none of POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces the fee. The rider's competing routes do not run: POL-NS-04 fails at limb (b) because the driver replied within 120 seconds (the 06:51:40 'Coming down now' was answered at 06:52:00, and he had already messaged at 06:50:35), and it also fails at limb (c) because the rider's own device sat about 519 m from the pin with 0 qualifying fixes; POL-NS-05's false-marker test is not met (about 24 m from the pin and stationary at 0.0 km/h at the arrival event, and the first in-geofence fix actually precedes the marker); and POL-NS-06 shows no shortfall (330 seconds held against a 300-second minimum, one unbroken run).

The escalation displaces that outcome.

ledger.claim: POL-NS-09(c) is a mandatory escalation trigger on this record. rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2 and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2, so two or more no-show disputes between this same rider and this same driver fall inside the trailing 90 days — which is exactly what the rider means when the claim says this is 'another dispute with the same driver'. A single trip's record cannot fairly resolve a repeat pairwise conflict in either direction, so the case must go to a human reviewer rather than be closed by the automated pipeline.

Escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal and, per POL-GEN-03, replaces any monetary ruling: the disputed amount is held rather than collected or refunded, and the rider's claim is not disposed of against the rider while review is pending. The fare breakdown shows the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee sitting at payment_status PENDING, charged_at null and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so an escalated file leaves the rider carrying no charge at all.

The in-app log shows the rider engaging on the pickup during the waiting window — 'Coming down now' sent at 06:51:40, answered by the driver's 'Okay, waiting' at 06:52:00 — and the driver cancelling three and a half minutes later at 06:55:30. That is a live coordination conflict between a repeat rider-driver pair, which is precisely the pattern POL-NS-09(c) reserves for human review instead of an automated single-case disposition.

EV-ADVIS-09110-01 is MISSING — issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, BLOCKING severity, weight_multiplier 0.0 — so no traffic advisory exists for this pickup road or waiting window. The driver therefore cannot credit any advisory-permitted accumulation under POL-NS-06(i): the in-geofence dwell stands on the trace alone, and no lawful-obstruction argument can be built on an artifact that carries no payload. I disclose the impairment and its issue code as POL-GEN-02 requires.

The driver's own GPS trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for the whole waiting window: all 34 driver fixes sit roughly 24 m from the pickup pin (min 24.01 m, max 24.01 m) at a constant 0.0 km/h, and all 34 pass the 25 m accuracy filter as qualifying in-radius fixes, so POL-NS-02 is satisfied and POL-NS-01 limb (b) is met. Because he was inside the radius rather than outside it, the wrong-entrance route in POL-NS-03 is not engaged at all.

The dwell is a single continuous in-geofence hold of 330 seconds, running from the first qualifying fix at 06:50:00 to the last at 06:55:30 — 30 seconds more than the 300-second minimum for a STANDARD pickup — so POL-NS-01 limb (c) is carried, and the record shows a -30.0 second shortfall basis, i.e. a surplus, not a shortfall.

The trip record carries the driver 'arrived' event at 06:50:20 and terminates the trip driver-side at 06:55:30 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the required dwell had elapsed, with no boarding event recorded — POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) are both satisfied.

There is no false arrival marker under POL-NS-05: at the 06:50:20 arrival event the trace puts the driver about 24 m from the pin and stationary at 0.0 km/h, nowhere near the 300 m distance trigger or the 15 km/h speed trigger, and the in-geofence fix at 06:50:00 actually precedes the marker, so the arrival timestamp is honest rather than premature.

The rider-exonerating clause POL-NS-04 cannot run on this record: the driver answered the rider's 06:51:40 message 'Coming down now.' with 'Okay, waiting.' at 06:52:00 — 20 seconds later, well inside the 120 second window — and he had already posted 'At Block 612 lobby pickup.' at 06:50:35, so limb (b) fails and the clause does not apply.

Independently, the rider's own device was never at the pickup point: all 16 rider fixes sit about 519 m from the pin, more than five times the 100 m STANDARD rider presence radius, and 0 rider fixes qualify, so POL-NS-04 limb (c) is affirmatively failed on admissible fixes and any residual issue falls back to POL-NS-01.

With POL-NS-01 carried in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 pays the driver 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee itemised in the ledger — SGD 3.20 — and the anti-farming guard is not tripped: 1 no-show termination in 30 days is below the threshold of 4, and 1/120 completed trips is 0.008, below 0.08.

The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09110-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — I disclose that impairment and do not rest on it. It is irrelevant here because the 330 second hold is one unbroken in-geofence run, so no accumulation of separate intervals under POL-NS-06(i) is needed to reach the minimum.
